findings.evidence: Running 'python3 -I jobs/pothier/pothier.py try <copy>.json --hints' prints 'decides 146; contradicted 2'. Both contradictions are of kind acted_on_after_lead_end. EO:610 (B21, no, 1907-04-06) has edge SH-bdbb6b2087da: EO 2022 of 1914-08-14 'Amends Executive Order 496 ... and Executive Order 610' (a Wikisource note). EO:7062 (B20, no, 1935-06-05) has edges SH-3647e071d203 (EO 10000, 1948, adding posts to the list 'established by Executive Order No. 5644 ... and by Executive Order No. 7062') and SH-117996891a66 / SH-99fb1b72ba35 (1961 FR entries). Under P2 these later acts are events of the parent, so the contradictions can be explained, but the doctrine reports that there are none.
findings.fix: Report 'contradicted 2' and state for EO 610 and EO 7062 why each later amendment is a later event of the parent (the Consular Regulations and Instructions; the EO 5644 list) under P2, rather than evidence that the amending order still commands.

findings.claim: EO 2022 only amends the Consular Regulations, the Instructions or the Tariff, so it merges into the parent on issue (P2).
findings.evidence: The held text (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-2022-temporarily-abolishing-fees-for-passports-and-providing-for.txt) also contains standing commands of its own outside the amended paragraphs: 'This order shall have no effect as to fees collected by diplomatic or consular officers before they shall have actually received notice of its contents. The Secretary of State may, when he sees fit, without further authorization, terminate the waiver of fees hereby put into effect, and restore the tariff of fees to the condition existing prior to the amendments made herein.' The fee waivers run 'until further notice'. P2 applies 'only when the member's own text shows that amending is its only operative content.' The doctrine itself keeps EO 2730 ('during the continuance of the war and until further orders') open in O5.
findings.fix: Remove EO:2022 from B21 and leave it open (for example in O5, as a standing fee directive with a delegated power to end the waiver), with the gap that the instrument or Secretary of State action ending the waiver is not held. Counts become 113 no, 145 decided, 118 open.

findings.claim: 'The project holds every source on which a no or yes lead rests.'
findings.evidence: B01 (32 yes leads) lists S2 (the eCFR versioner) among its sources, and S2 is held: false. The engine adds 'source S2 ... is not yet held' to each B01 lead. I confirmed S2's content on the web: the latest amendment of 101.3 is dated 2023-11-16, with an issue date of 2024-06-24.
findings.fix: Say that every no lead rests on held sources, and that the yes leads rest on held S1 plus S2, which was read on the web and is not held.

findings.claim: Under P4 (PD-CS-ONE-PERSON), a one-person order gets a no lead only when its own terms fix the end or a quoted fact bounds the person's life. Disability retirements without a stated effective date (EO 4279-A, EO 4285) therefore stay open.
findings.evidence: The doctrine cites no held text for this rule (PD-CS-ONE-PERSON lives in research/pothier/doctrines/, which this review may not open). The held S16 (TR-CANAL-ZONE) pin says one-person orders are 'spent on issue rather than swept'. The texts of EO 4279-A and EO 4285 order the retirement with no future date and no condition, so on the S16 convention each would take effect on issue. Keeping them open is conservative, but the stated rule is unsupported by any held source, and it sits uneasily beside B17, which treats a dated retirement as an act performed on its date.
findings.fix: Quote the PD-CS-ONE-PERSON rule that keeps an undated one-person retirement open. Otherwise decide EO 4279-A and EO 4285 as no, TERM, spent on issue, with order_date, and keep only EO 7358 (effective on unheld Senate confirmation) open.

findings.claim: EO 5577's only operative content is a revocation, so it is spent on issue (P1).
findings.evidence: S3 (EO_5577.txt): EO 5011 'is hereby revoked, and, effective immediately, the said places are restored to and included within the port limits of San Francisco'. The second clause fixes the limits of a continuing port. The doctrine keeps other port-limit orders open in O1 (for example EO 5578 of the same day, which changes the designation of the San Francisco port and extends its limits). P1 counts a restoration as single-act only when it keeps no continuing condition. A redrawing of a port's limits is closer to a limits order than to a restoration of land to the public domain.
findings.fix: Either justify the treatment (for example, that the San Francisco-Oakland limits now rest on CBP Dec. 06-23 under 19 CFR 101.3, which is not an end of EO 5577 under P3) and leave EO 5577 open in O1, or explain why restoring places to port limits counts as a pure restoration under P1.

findings.location: Branch B18 basis and mechanism M3
findings.claim: Under P1, an order that only abolishes ports of entry is spent on issue.
findings.evidence: P1 names orders that only 'revoke another order, restore land to the public domain, or relinquish a reservation'. Abolishing a port is not among them. P7 covers the abolition of a member's subject by a later instrument, not the abolishing order itself. The extension is reasonable: I read all 38 B18 texts, and each only abolishes or discontinues named ports, with an effective date at most about a month after the order. It is still the author's extension and not the coordinator's ruling.
findings.fix: Label B18 as an extension of P1 to port abolitions and list it as an adoption question for the owner.

wrong_member_decisions.why: The text has operative content beyond amending: fee waivers 'until further notice', a clause tying the order's effect to notice, and a delegation letting the Secretary of State terminate the waiver. P2 does not apply, and the member should be open (R5).
The lead is right, but its date is wrong: the JSON fixes 1931-06-08 although EO 5644 makes the cancellation effective July 1, 1931 (R2).

Questionable: besides revoking EO 5011, it restores named places to the San Francisco port limits, a continuing limits provision. That is not clearly a pure revocation or restoration under P1. The doctrine keeps comparable limits orders, such as EO 5578 of the same day, open (R10).

summary: The doctrine's structure is sound. The 32 yes leads rest on a verified current-law predicate: every member number in B01 is cited in the held April 2025 text of 19 CFR 101.3(b)(1), and the eCFR history shows no amendment after 2023-11-16. The later-instrument ends in B02-B12 are verified against held texts that reach each member by number, by date and subject, or by abolishing the member's only port. Pins and hashes match for every held source except S23. Five errors must be fixed before adoption. The superseding visa order is EO 5435, not EO 5345. B09's JSON dates the EO 5644 cancellation to 1931-06-08 instead of its stated effective date, 1931-07-01. S8's Federal Register page is 1 FR 1737, not 1502. The engine reports 2 contradictions with held edges (EO 610, EO 7062), but the md says there are none. EO 2022 carries operative commands beyond amendment and should be open, not merged into its parent under P2. Smaller corrections: update S23 and use P7 for the port-abolition branches; fix the location of EO 4284 in section (d); correct the statement that all yes/no sources are held; support or revise the O6p rule for undated one-person retirements; reconsider EO 5577's limits clause; tidy the undecidable list and the B16 end date.
